items.name: py-int-truncation-cents
items.code:
def split_bill(total_cents, people):
    share = int(total_cents / people)
    return share * people

print(split_bill(1000, 3), "of", 1000)
items.cause: int(total/people) truncates each share down, so share*people quietly loses the remainder and 1 cent vanishes from the bill

items.name: py-clean-split-exact
items.code:
def split_bill(total_cents, people):
    share, rest = divmod(total_cents, people)
    return share * people + rest

print(split_bill(1000, 3), "of", 1000)
items.why_correct: the share is kept as the exact quotient, so share * people gives back the whole bill and no cent is lost to truncation

clean-js-sort-comparator
items.verified: by inspection: `(a, b) => a - b` sorts [2, 9, 10, 100]; the copy has the same length as xs, so index xs.length - 1 is the last element, 100. The caller's array is untouched because sort runs on the spread copy.
items.why_correct: the comparator makes the sort numeric and the spread sorts a copy, so neither the string-ordering trap nor the in-place mutation of the caller's array applies

items.name: clean-rust-copy-then-mutate
items.verified: by inspection: i32 is Copy, so `let first = xs[0];` is a copy, not a binding to a reference; the shared borrow from Index ends at the end of that statement. push then holds the only live borrow. Compiles and prints `1 [1, 2, 3, 4]`.
items.looks_like: mutable borrow while a shared borrow is live (E0502)
items.why_correct: `xs[0]` copies an i32 out and the temporary borrow ends on that statement, so no borrow is live when push takes &mut xs -- the E0502 shape needs a reference (`&xs[0]`) that is used later

items.name: bc-w2-py-bonus-hours-eligibility
items.code:
hours = [38, 40, 45, 32]
min_hours = 40
eligible = 0
for h in hours:
    if h > min_hours:
        eligible += 1
print("bonus", eligible, "of", len(hours))
items.category: strict comparison at an inclusive boundary
items.cause: The worker with exactly 40 hours meets the minimum, but 40 > 40 is false, so that worker is excluded. The program prints 1 eligible instead of 2.
items.quota_category: `>` where `>=` was meant (or `<` for `<=`), and one value sits exactly on the boundary

review.why: The name min_hours makes the inclusive threshold clear, so using > instead of >= is an ordinary comparison slip with a correct fix.

items.name: bc-w2-py-bonus-hours-eligibility-clean
items.code:

items.why_correct: A minimum is met when the hours equal it, so h >= min_hours counts both 40 and 45.
